text:
lisa_finance: Heads-up 1: BatchOps sent a follow-up with contract terms. A few invoice & billing items look off to finance. Can we quick-validate before I send to legal?

omar_procure: Which items? Are we talking net terms, currency, or invoicing frequency?

lisa_finance: All of the above. Snapshot from their term sheet: invoice monthly in USD, net-45, one-time onboarding fee $15k (non-refundable), price experiments clause allowing +/- 15% price changes to "optimize platform economics" with 30-day notice.

sarah_ops: That price experiment clause worries me. If they can up our embedding or GPU rates mid-contractor with notice, our committed budgeting goes sideways.

henry_legal: We should push to remove any unilateral price change clause. At minimum: require mutual agreement for price increases within the first 12 months or automatic termination without penalty if material (>5%) hikes.

lisa_finance: Also flagged: billing is monthly but they require payment in USD wired to an EU entity (FX risk). Ask for invoice in customerurrency or net-60 if they insist on USD.

omar_procure: We can request monthly invoicing with Net-30 standard. Net-45 is okay if we get early-pay discount? But finance prefers vendor discounts rather than longer net.

devon_sales: From their side: onboarding fee covers seat configuration + SSO integration. They said it could be credited back as usage credit if we exceed Tier B commits in the first 6 months. Might be negotiable.

lisa_finance: Good to know. Propose counter: onboarding fee converted to usage credit prorated over 6 months if usage >= 80% of committed in that window.

henry_legal: Add: SLA credits for downtime should be credited as invoice line items and adjustable against the upcoming invoice, not a separate credit note. Also require clear definition of "downtime" and measurement method.

sarah_ops: Operational ask: include monthly usage export in CSV and billing mapping by SKU (vGPU hrs, embedding vector-hours, storage, network). We need to reconcile automated billing vs telemetry.

lisa_finance: Yeah reconcile is critical. We should request a sample invoice template before signing.

omar_procure: On currency/FX: ask for an option to be invoiced in USD or our billing currency (USD preferred) but payments via ACH in USD to our US entity; if not possible, require a fixed FX rate in contract to avoid surprises for 12 months.

devon_sales: I'll ask for a price-protection clause for 12 months and push to cap any experiment-based increases to max 5% with mutual consent.

henry_legal: Also include a termination for convenience with 60 days notice and pro-rated return of any prepaid unused committed hours. No abortive fees for early exit during the trial/pilot.

lisa_finance: On audit rights: include a quarterly audit window where we can verify vector-hour counts against our telemetry. If discrepancies > 2%, require adjustment and reimbursement.

sarah_ops: Add technical appendix: define embedding vector-hour precisely (is it per vector emitted, per vector-dimension, per partial batch?) and whether dedup/caching reduces billed units.

omar_procure: I'll consolidate asks into an initial redline. Target: send to vendor by EOD tomorrow. Procurement_bot: tag "vendor-contract" and set decision milestone 2024-07-01.

procurement_bot: Tagged vendor-contract. Reminder: attach term sheet and sample invoices to the contract packet.

lisa_finance: One more ask: require monthly invoice line-itemization plus an API endpoint for real-time usage if they have one. That makes reconciliation easier.

devon_sales: They do have a usage API but rate-limited; I'll ask for a higher SLA on the usage API for enterprise customers.

henry_legal: I'll draft contract language for price protection, FX handling, SLA credit mechanics, and audit rights. Omar, loop me into the redline.

omar_procure: Will do. Sending draft to the group in ~2 hours for a quick review.

lisa_finance: Thanks all  let's try to finalize negotiation points before the pilot starts.

devon_sales: Note for vendor: if they want a quicker signature, offer a short-term pilot PO with capped exposure (max $X) while we work contract terms. Might speed up procurement.

sarah_ops: Agree. Pilot PO with capped spend and explicit overage opt-out.

lisa_finance: I'll propose a pilot PO cap of $30k and require overage opt-out switch in the console that prevents billing beyond cap.

omar_procure: Great, adding that option. Draft out and I'll send.

procurement_bot: Reminder: attach pilots and PO templates to Confluence under vendor-evals/BatchOps. Deadline: 2024-06-30.
